newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek rates keep falling, ecu/drs ranges, bonds hold.
newsitem.headline: Greek rates keep falling, ecu/drs ranges, bonds hold.

text.p: Greek depos and forex forwards receded further in late quiet trading and bonds were steady, digesting earlier gains as ecu/drachma hovering around 311, dealers said.

"Depo rates and implied drachma rates from forex forwards are coming down fast after the central bank fixing," a dealer at a foreign bank said. "Rates have fallen another 10 to 20 basis points after the fixing."
Dealers said they expected interbank interest rates to head lower as market conditions were returning to normal and the drachma was holding its ground against the ecu.
"Ecu/drachma hugs 311 in late dealings," said a dealer at a foreign bank.
The central bank sold about $50 million for drachmas in its early morning intervention driving ecu/drachma as low as 310.0/40, dealers said.

Ecu/drachma steadied around 110.60/80 going into the fixing and settled at 311, down from Thursday's 312, with the central bank and a large state commercial bank selling small amounts of ecus for drachmas.

The Bank of Greece also sold about 60 million French francs for drachmas at the fixing. Traders said this could signal preparations for joint intervention by EU central banks on Monday to help the franc.

"The central bank's move to sell French francs aggressively was a surprise," said a forex dealer. "It could be that the Bank of Greece wanted to be short francs in order to buy them back on Monday, possibly in the context of a concerted EU intervention."
Bonds were in a consolidation bout in late dealings, digesting earlier gains.

"Bonds are little changed in late trade after today's mini-rally on the back of a stronger drachma and falling interbank rates," a trader said. "Bond prices are likely to recover further if the drachma continues to hold and funding cost eases."
